title: Polynomial-time comparison of unary values
statement: Let $f,g$ be natural-valued functions on Boolean words. If the unary encodings of both $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ are polynomial-time computable, then the function mapping $x$ to the one-bit word that is true exactly when $f(x)\le g(x)$ is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: the unary encoding of $f(x)$ is polynomial-time computable
the unary encoding of $g(x)$ is polynomial-time computable
replaced: If two unary values are polynomial-time computable, then the single-bit test deciding whether the first is at most the second is polynomial-time computable, by charged subtraction followed by a finite empty-word test.
